title: US midterm elections — House, one third of the Senate, 36 governorships
source: NEWS: contemporaneous coverage of the Collins-Murray CR deal (NBC/CBS/PBS/WaPo/The Hill, early Aug 2026), which is explicitly built to fund the government past the midterms; the date itself is statutory (first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of an even year = 2026-11-03, a Tuesday) but no primary source was fetched, checked 2026-08-29
notes: Not a print — a dated policy checkpoint, and the causal driver behind the FY2027 funding timeline: the Senate CR runs to Dec 11 precisely so the full-year fight lands in a lame-duck session shaped by this result. Filed `estimate` per the event-research lane's no-self-confirm limit even though the date is statutory — the honest reading is date-certain, outcome-unknown. Discovered during the government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 initial research; the CR's own expiry (Dec 4 or Dec 11) is a second dated checkpoint left un-proposed until the chambers reconcile which.
